title: Management responsibility for information security (ISMS.1.A1)
description: The institutional management bears overall responsibility for information security and must ensure that an information security process is established, implemented, maintained, and continually improved. Management must actively support the information security officer, approve the security policy, and ensure adequate resources are provided for information security. This is the foundational Basis requirement for any IT-Grundschutz implementation.
remediation_hint: Obtain formal management endorsement of the security programme; document it in the security policy and review it at least annually; include information security in management reporting.

title: Information security policy (ISMS.1.A3)
description: A written information security policy, approved by management, must be established and communicated to all staff. The policy must define the objectives and scope of information security, management's commitment to the programme, and the organisational framework. The policy must be reviewed at defined intervals and following significant changes.
remediation_hint: Draft and publish the security policy with explicit management sign-off; establish an annual review cycle; provide staff with acknowledgement of having read the policy.

title: Appointment of an information security officer (ISMS.1.A4)
description: An information security officer (ISO) must be appointed with sufficient authority, resources, and access to ensure the information security process is established across the institution. The ISO must be given adequate time and support and must be able to escalate to management without obstruction. The appointment must be formally documented.
remediation_hint: Formalise the ISO appointment in writing; define scope of authority; ensure the role is distinct from operational IT management to preserve independence.

title: Defining security measures (ISMS.1.A6)
description: Security measures necessary to protect information assets in scope must be identified, documented, implemented, and their status tracked. The selection of measures must be risk-driven and aligned with the applicable Bausteine from the BSI IT-Grundschutz Kompendium. Outstanding measures must be tracked in a remediation plan with owners and target dates.
remediation_hint: Complete the IT-Grundschutz modelling for all target objects; assign owners to each measure; track open items in a remediation register with defined completion dates.

title: Integrating staff into the security process (ISMS.1.A8)
description: All staff must be made aware of information security requirements relevant to their role. Mandatory awareness training must be provided at onboarding and at regular intervals thereafter. Staff must be informed of the escalation path for security incidents and of their responsibilities during the incident response process.
remediation_hint: Implement a mandatory onboarding security briefing and annual refresher; record completion; include contractor and third-party personnel in the programme.

title: Roles and responsibilities for information security (ORP.1.A1)
description: Roles and responsibilities for information security must be clearly defined, documented, and communicated to all relevant staff. All staff must know their information security obligations. Responsibilities must cover normal operations, incidents, and continuity events.
remediation_hint: Document an RACI for information security; publish it to all staff; review roles when the organisational structure changes.

title: Assignment of tasks and authorisations (ORP.1.A2)
description: Tasks and authorisations must be assigned in a consistent and documented manner. No single person should hold both the operational and auditing role for a critical process. Privileges must follow the principle of least privilege and must be periodically reviewed to detect and remove accumulation of rights.
remediation_hint: Review access rights at least annually; enforce least-privilege assignment at provisioning; separate duties for critical operations.

title: Documented operating procedures (ORP.1.A4)
description: Documented operating procedures must exist for all security-relevant processes including onboarding, offboarding, change management, incident response, and backup and recovery. Procedures must be accessible to responsible staff and must be kept current. A review cycle must be defined for each procedure.
remediation_hint: Maintain a living set of standard operating procedures in an accessible location; assign an owner to each procedure; establish and enforce an annual review cycle.

title: Regulated procedures for onboarding new staff (ORP.2.A1)
description: A defined onboarding process must ensure that new staff, including temporary staff and contractors, receive the access rights, equipment, and security briefings required for their role. Access must be provisioned only after identity verification and role assignment are complete. The process must be documented and applied consistently.
remediation_hint: Establish a joiner checklist that gates system access on role approval and security acknowledgement; include contractor and third-party staff.

title: Regulated procedures for offboarding departing staff (ORP.2.A2)
description: A defined offboarding process must ensure that all access rights are revoked promptly when staff leave or change role. Credentials, tokens, certificates, and physical access must all be covered. The process must apply equally to permanent and temporary staff and must be tested periodically.
remediation_hint: Implement an automated deprovisioning trigger on HR termination events; verify revocation within 24 hours; log the completion of each offboarding action.

title: Regulated use of external staff and contractors (ORP.2.A4)
description: External personnel must be subject to information security requirements equivalent to those applied to internal staff for the scope of their engagement. Non-disclosure agreements must be signed before access is granted. Access must be limited to the minimum necessary for the contracted task and must be reviewed regularly.
remediation_hint: Include security obligations in external staff contracts; maintain a register of active contractors with their access scope; revoke all access at contract end.

title: Identity and access management policy (ORP.4.A1)
description: A policy governing the management of identities, authentication, and access rights must be established and applied to all systems and applications in scope. The policy must address account lifecycle management, privileged access, authentication strength requirements, and the handling of service accounts.
remediation_hint: Write and approve an IAM policy; enforce it through periodic access reviews; align privileged access procedures with the policy.

title: User account and authorisation management (ORP.4.A2)
description: User accounts must be created, modified, and deleted through a documented, authorised process. All accounts must be assigned to a named individual; shared or anonymous accounts are prohibited except where technically unavoidable and explicitly approved. Unused accounts must be disabled after a defined inactivity period.
remediation_hint: Implement an automated account provisioning workflow; set an inactivity threshold of 90 days or less; run quarterly access certification campaigns.

title: Identification of legal and regulatory requirements (ORP.5.A1)
description: All legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements relevant to information security must be identified, documented, and their implications assessed. Requirements must include data protection obligations, sector-specific regulations, and contractual obligations from customer and partner agreements.
remediation_hint: Maintain a compliance register mapping each applicable law or regulation to a responsible owner; review at least annually and when the regulatory landscape changes.

title: Compliance monitoring (ORP.5.A2)
description: Regular checks must be performed to confirm that legal, regulatory, and policy requirements are being met. Non-compliance findings must be tracked and remediated within defined timescales. Results must be reported to management at appropriate intervals.
remediation_hint: Establish a compliance calendar with assigned owners; report compliance posture to management quarterly; track open gaps in the remediation register.

title: Definition of cryptographic requirements (CON.1.A1)
description: The requirements for cryptographic protection of data at rest, data in transit, and data in use must be defined in a cryptographic policy. The policy must specify acceptable algorithms, minimum key lengths, permitted protocols, and key management procedures. The BSI TR-02102 technical guideline must be used as the reference for algorithm selection.
remediation_hint: Adopt BSI TR-02102 for algorithm selection; enforce TLS 1.2 minimum (TLS 1.3 preferred) for all in-transit paths; document encryption coverage for all stores holding personal data.

title: Cryptographic key management (CON.1.A2)
description: Cryptographic keys must be generated, distributed, stored, rotated, and destroyed according to a defined key management procedure. Key material must be protected from unauthorised disclosure, substitution, and modification. Private keys must never be stored alongside the data they protect or in a form accessible to application code at rest.
remediation_hint: Use a dedicated key management service (KMS) or Hardware Security Module (HSM) for key storage; define and test key rotation schedules; prohibit software-level plaintext key storage.

title: Cryptographic protection of stored data (CON.1.A4)
description: Data classified as confidential or above must be protected by encryption at rest using approved algorithms as defined in the cryptographic policy (CON.1.A1). Encrypted backups must use keys that are distinct from the live data encryption keys. The coverage of at-rest encryption must be documented for each data store.
remediation_hint: Enable volume or field-level encryption for all stores holding personal data; verify no plaintext copy exists in any backup path; test decryption as part of recovery drills.

title: Obligation to data protection (CON.2.A1)
description: All staff who handle personal data must be formally committed to data protection obligations. This commitment must cover applicable data protection legislation, the institution's data protection policy, and the consequences of non-compliance. A data protection officer must be appointed where required by law, and their independence must be ensured.
remediation_hint: Appoint a data protection officer (or document why appointment is not legally required); maintain signed data protection commitments for all relevant staff; confirm DPO independence.

title: Backup requirements analysis (CON.3.A1)
description: The recovery point objective (RPO) and recovery time objective (RTO) must be determined for each information asset based on its criticality and business impact. Requirements must be documented and reviewed when the system or its data classification changes. Results must inform the backup concept (CON.3.A2).
remediation_hint: Conduct and document a business impact analysis for each application; confirm RPO and RTO with the application owner; align backup frequency and retention with the agreed objectives.

title: Backup concept (CON.3.A2)
description: A backup concept must define the scope, frequency, retention period, storage media, and off-site or out-of-region placement for all backups. The concept must address backup of all system and application data required to recover to the agreed RPO. Backup of configuration data must be included.
remediation_hint: Write and approve a backup concept; verify it covers all in-scope systems including databases, object storage, and configuration; confirm off-site or out-of-region placement for at least one copy.

title: Minimum data backup requirements (CON.3.A3)
description: All relevant data must be backed up at a frequency that meets the agreed RPO. Backup completeness and integrity must be verified automatically. Backup media and destinations must be protected against unauthorised access and environmental hazards to a standard equivalent to the source systems.
remediation_hint: Automate backup jobs and configure alerting on failure; perform monthly restore tests and document the outcome; encrypt backup media with keys distinct from the live data keys.

title: Information security requirements for software procurement (CON.6.A1)
description: Information security requirements must be defined before procuring software or cloud services. Requirements must cover authentication, access control, audit logging, cryptographic capabilities, and data residency. Security requirements must be included as contractual criteria and verified before contract signature.
remediation_hint: Maintain a security requirements checklist for procurement; include it in every request for proposal and contract review; obtain evidence of compliance before go-live.

title: Secure software deployment (CON.6.A2)
description: Software and configuration changes must be deployed through a documented, authorised process. Deployments must be authorised, tested in a non-production environment, and capable of being rolled back if they introduce security regressions. Deployment logs must be retained for a defined minimum period.
remediation_hint: Implement a CI/CD pipeline with gated security tests; require explicit approval for production deployments; retain deployment audit logs for at least 90 days.

title: Defining security requirements for software development (CON.8.A1)
description: Information security requirements must be defined and integrated into the software development lifecycle from the requirements phase. Requirements must address authentication, authorisation, session management, input validation, error handling, and cryptographic protection of sensitive data. Requirements must be verified at each development gate.
remediation_hint: Publish secure development standards aligned to OWASP ASVS or equivalent; run mandatory security review gates at requirements, design, and pre-release phases; track deviations as risks.

title: Software acceptance and release process (CON.8.A2)
description: Software must pass defined security acceptance criteria before release to production. Acceptance criteria must include security tests, vulnerability scans, and code review. Deviations from acceptance criteria must be risk-accepted by a named authority and documented before release.
remediation_hint: Define security acceptance gates in the release checklist; require a named security sign-off before production deployment; log each release decision with the accepting authority.

title: Test data protection (CON.8.A7)
description: Production data must not be used for development or testing purposes unless there is no viable alternative and appropriate technical and organisational measures are in place. Where use of production data is unavoidable, it must be pseudonymised or anonymised before use, access must be restricted to the minimum necessary, and the use must be explicitly authorised.
remediation_hint: Establish a test data management process; generate synthetic or anonymised test datasets; document any approved use of production data with DPO sign-off.

title: Change management concept (OPS.1.1.2.A1)
description: A documented change management process must govern all changes to IT systems, applications, and configurations. The process must cover request, risk assessment, authorisation, implementation, and post-implementation review. Emergency change procedures must be defined and applied only in genuine emergencies.
remediation_hint: Implement a change management workflow covering standard, normal, and emergency change categories; require risk impact assessment for all normal and emergency changes.

title: Maintaining operations during changes (OPS.1.1.2.A2)
description: Changes must be planned to minimise disruption to normal operations. Where possible, changes must be deployed in defined maintenance windows. Rollback plans must be defined and tested before deployment. Significant changes must be rehearsed in a non-production environment representative of production.
remediation_hint: Define maintenance windows; require a tested rollback plan for all non-standard changes; conduct a post-change review within 48 hours of each significant deployment.

title: Secure change testing (OPS.1.1.2.A3)
description: All changes must be tested prior to deployment in a test environment that is representative of the production environment. Security regression tests must be included in the test suite for changes to security-relevant components. Test results must be documented and linked to the change record.
remediation_hint: Maintain a dedicated staging environment; require test sign-off before production deployment; include security regression tests in the automated test suite.

title: Patch and vulnerability management concept (OPS.1.1.3.A1)
description: A documented patch and vulnerability management concept must define the process for identifying, assessing, prioritising, and remediating vulnerabilities across all IT components in scope. The concept must specify escalation paths for critical vulnerabilities and the maximum time-to-patch per severity class.
remediation_hint: Publish and approve a patch management policy with time-to-patch SLAs (critical: 48 hours, high: 30 days); assign an owner per vulnerability class; document the escalation path.

title: Regular scanning for known vulnerabilities (OPS.1.1.3.A2)
description: All IT systems and applications in scope must be regularly scanned for known vulnerabilities using automated tooling. Scan results must be documented, triaged, and fed into the remediation workflow. The scan schedule must be at least as frequent as the patch management SLAs require.
remediation_hint: Deploy continuous vulnerability scanning (SAST, DAST, SCA) in the CI pipeline; generate weekly posture reports; feed confirmed vulnerabilities into the remediation tracker automatically.

title: Timely application of security patches (OPS.1.1.3.A3)
description: Security patches must be applied within the time limits defined in the patch management concept. Critical and high-severity patches must be prioritised over other maintenance activities. Where patching is temporarily infeasible, a compensating control must be documented and approved by the information security officer.
remediation_hint: Automate patch deployment for OS and runtime images in the CI/CD pipeline; track outstanding patches by severity class; escalate unpatched critical items to management within the defined SLA window.

title: Backup and recovery concept (OPS.1.1.5.A1)
description: A comprehensive backup and recovery concept must define the scope, schedules, retention periods, media types, and recovery procedures for all systems in scope. The concept must be aligned with the RPO and RTO requirements from the backup requirements analysis (CON.3.A1) and reviewed at defined intervals.
remediation_hint: Align the operational backup configuration with the approved concept; automate alerting on backup failures; store at least one backup copy in a separate security zone from the primary systems.

title: Backup of key configuration data (OPS.1.1.5.A3)
description: Configuration data essential for system recovery including application configuration, infrastructure-as-code definitions, secrets references, and certificate metadata must be backed up separately from application data and stored securely. Configuration backup must be tested as part of recovery drills.
remediation_hint: Version-control all infrastructure configuration in a separate repository; include configuration restore in the recovery runbook; test configuration restore at least once per quarter.

title: Restore testing and documentation (OPS.1.1.5.A4)
description: Recovery procedures must be tested at regular intervals to verify that data can be restored within the agreed RTO. Test results must be documented including the time taken and the completeness of the recovered data. Failures must be tracked and remediated before the next test cycle.
remediation_hint: Schedule and run quarterly restore tests across all backup tiers; document the time taken and data completeness; report test outcomes to the information security officer.

title: Cloud usage strategy (OPS.2.2.A1)
description: A documented cloud usage strategy must be established defining which data types, workloads, and processes may be processed in cloud environments, which cloud service and deployment models are permissible, and which data residency and sovereignty requirements must be satisfied. The strategy must be approved by management.
remediation_hint: Write and approve a cloud usage policy explicitly addressing data classification, residency, and sovereign cloud requirements; review when a new cloud service is onboarded or the regulatory context changes.

title: Classification of cloud service criticality (OPS.2.2.A2)
description: Cloud services used by the institution must be classified according to their criticality and the sensitivity of data they process. The classification must drive the appropriate level of security controls, due diligence requirements, and contractual obligations for each service.
remediation_hint: Maintain a cloud service inventory with criticality classification; apply more stringent vetting to services processing personal or sensitive data; review the inventory when services are added or changed.

title: Security requirements for cloud service providers (OPS.2.2.A3)
description: Minimum security requirements must be defined for cloud service providers handling organisational data. Requirements must address certifications (BSI C5, ISO 27001, or SOC 2 Type II), data residency commitments, subprocessor transparency, audit rights, and incident notification obligations.
remediation_hint: Define a minimum certification bar for cloud providers processing personal data; require evidence of compliance before onboarding; reassess annually and at each contract renewal.

title: Cloud service agreement and data processing contract (OPS.2.2.A4)
description: A written agreement must be in place with each cloud service provider covering information security obligations, data processing terms compliant with applicable data protection law, incident reporting obligations, audit rights, and exit provisions. The agreement must be reviewed before each contract renewal.
remediation_hint: Review all cloud provider contracts for the required clauses before go-live; ensure DPA terms cover all personal data processing; track contract renewal dates in the compliance calendar.

title: Cloud-native service security baseline (OPS.2.3.A1)
description: Cloud-native services including managed databases, message queues, serverless functions, and object storage must be configured in accordance with the provider's published security baseline and any applicable CIS benchmark or equivalent hardening guide. Default configurations that expose public endpoints or disable encryption must be explicitly overridden before deployment.
remediation_hint: Run infrastructure-as-code security scanning (tfsec, checkov, or equivalent) on all cloud resource definitions; block deployments that fail mandatory security checks; review benchmark compliance quarterly.

title: Detection concept (DER.1.A1)
description: A concept for the detection of security-relevant events must be established. The concept must define which event sources are monitored, what constitutes a security event requiring response, the responsible parties for detection, and the escalation path to the incident management process. The concept must be reviewed annually.
remediation_hint: Document the detection concept; map it to the incident response procedure; review and update when significant infrastructure changes are made.

title: Central logging (DER.1.A2)
description: Security-relevant events must be logged centrally. Log sources must include authentication events, privileged access, system and application errors, network perimeter events, and changes to security configuration. Logs must be protected from tampering and retained for a defined minimum period appropriate to incident investigation timelines.
remediation_hint: Deploy centralised log aggregation (SIEM or equivalent); enforce log retention of at least 90 days active and 12 months archived for audit-relevant events; protect log integrity with write-once storage or cryptographic sealing.

title: Alert thresholds and escalation (DER.1.A3)
description: Alert rules must be configured for high-priority security events including authentication failures, privilege escalation, unexpected outbound connections, and availability degradation. Alerts must be routed to the responsible team and escalated to incident management if not acknowledged within a defined timeframe.
remediation_hint: Define and test alert rules for each event class; establish on-call routing and acknowledgement SLAs; test alerting end-to-end at least quarterly using synthetic events.

title: Incident management concept (DER.2.1.A1)
description: A documented incident management concept must define the classification of security incidents, roles and responsibilities for detection and response, escalation procedures, communication requirements (internal and to supervisory authorities), and criteria for incident closure. The concept must be tested through tabletop exercises.
remediation_hint: Write and test the incident response plan; ensure the plan covers personal data breaches explicitly with notification timelines; rehearse with a tabletop exercise at least annually.

title: Incident classification and prioritisation (DER.2.1.A2)
description: Security incidents must be classified and prioritised according to their impact, urgency, and scope. Classification criteria must be documented and applied consistently. Personal data breaches must be identified as a distinct incident class that triggers data protection notification obligations under applicable law.
remediation_hint: Define a severity matrix with clear escalation thresholds; train first responders on breach identification criteria; integrate breach detection rules into the SIEM alert set.

title: Incident documentation and post-incident review (DER.2.1.A3)
description: All security incidents must be documented from detection through to closure. Documentation must capture timeline, impact, root cause, remediation actions taken, and lessons learned. A post-incident review must be conducted for significant incidents and findings fed back into the security programme.
remediation_hint: Use a structured incident record template; mandate post-incident review within 14 days of closure for high and critical incidents; track lessons-learned actions in the remediation register.

title: Internal audit planning (DER.3.1.A1)
description: Information security audits must be planned and conducted at defined intervals. The audit scope must cover all components identified in the IT-Grundschutz modelling. Audit findings must be tracked with assigned owners and remediated within defined timeframes.
remediation_hint: Publish an annual internal audit schedule; assign qualified auditors independent of the functions they audit; track findings in the remediation register with defined completion dates.

title: Auditing information security measures (DER.3.1.A2)
description: Implemented information security measures must be regularly audited for effectiveness. Audits must include both documentary review and technical testing. Results must be reported to management and used to improve the information security programme. Technical test findings must be fed into the remediation workflow.
remediation_hint: Include technical penetration testing and configuration review in the annual audit programme; present results to the CISO or equivalent; require management sign-off on the remediation plan.

title: Business continuity plan (DER.4.A1)
description: A business continuity plan (BCP) must be established covering the loss of IT services, key personnel, and critical infrastructure. The BCP must define recovery priorities, minimum service levels, and communication procedures for major incidents. The plan must be aligned with the RTO objectives defined in the backup requirements analysis.
remediation_hint: Write and approve the BCP; align recovery priorities with the business impact analysis; test the plan with a tabletop exercise annually and update it based on test findings.

title: Business continuity testing (DER.4.A2)
description: Business continuity and disaster recovery plans must be tested at defined intervals to verify that recovery objectives can be met. Test results must be documented and used to improve the plan. Critical staff must be trained on their continuity roles and the current contact list must be maintained.
remediation_hint: Conduct an annual BCP test; document the outcome and identify gaps; ensure that key recovery personnel have been briefed and the contact directory is current.

title: Authentication for web applications and services (APP.3.1.A1)
description: Web applications and web services must enforce strong authentication for all users accessing sensitive functions or data. Default credentials must be changed before deployment. Authentication mechanisms must be resistant to common attacks including brute force, credential stuffing, and session fixation. Privileged access must require multi-factor authentication.
remediation_hint: Implement multi-factor authentication for all privileged access; enforce account lockout after a defined number of failed attempts; use standard, well-reviewed authentication libraries.

title: Access control for web applications (APP.3.1.A2)
description: Access control in web applications must enforce the principle of least privilege. Every function and data object must have a server-side access control check. Access control decisions must not rely solely on client-supplied parameters. Horizontal and vertical privilege escalation must be tested as part of the security acceptance process.
remediation_hint: Implement server-side authorisation for every sensitive endpoint; audit access control coverage with automated testing; document the access control matrix for each user role.

title: Secure error and exception handling (APP.3.1.A3)
description: Web applications must not return stack traces, internal error messages, or technical details to end users. Error messages presented to users must be generic and must not reveal information about system architecture, database schema, or internal identifiers. Detailed diagnostic information must be logged server-side only and protected from unauthorised access.
remediation_hint: Replace default error pages with custom generic messages; configure the application to suppress stack traces in production mode; review error handling as part of security code review.

title: Input validation for web applications (APP.3.1.A6)
description: All input received by web applications from users, APIs, and external services must be validated against expected type, length, format, and range before processing. Validation must be performed server-side. Parameterised queries or prepared statements must be used for all database interactions to prevent injection attacks.
remediation_hint: Implement a centralised input validation layer; enforce parameterised queries throughout the data access layer; include input fuzzing in the automated security test suite.

title: Database access control (APP.4.3.A1)
description: Access to databases must be restricted to authorised applications and users. Each application must use a dedicated database account with the minimum permissions required for its function. Direct user access to production databases must require explicit authorisation and must be logged. Superuser credentials must not be used by application code.
remediation_hint: Assign each application its own database user with least-privilege schema grants; prohibit shared superuser credentials in application connection strings; log and alert on direct DBA access to production.

title: Minimal database configuration (APP.4.3.A2)
description: Database instances must be configured with the minimal set of services and features enabled. Unused stored procedures, remote administration features, and sample schemas must be disabled or removed. The database management system must run under a dedicated low-privilege service account and must not be reachable from general user networks.
remediation_hint: Apply the CIS benchmark for the relevant DBMS; disable the remote administration interface in production; run the DBMS service under a non-root, non-administrator account.

title: Database transaction security (APP.4.3.A3)
description: Database transactions must be designed to maintain data integrity under concurrent access. Appropriate transaction isolation levels must be selected for each workload and documented. Partial write failures must not leave data in an inconsistent state; rollback procedures must be tested as part of recovery drills.
remediation_hint: Select transaction isolation levels intentionally and document the rationale; include concurrency and failure injection tests in the test suite; verify rollback behaviour during restore drills.

title: Container orchestration security policy (APP.4.4.A1)
description: A security policy for container orchestration platforms (Kubernetes or equivalent) must be established covering role-based access control, network policies, pod security standards, image provenance controls, and secrets management. Default orchestration configurations that are insecure must be overridden before workload deployment.
remediation_hint: Apply a pod security standard (at minimum Baseline, prefer Restricted); deploy network policies to restrict pod-to-pod communication; use an external secrets manager rather than plain Kubernetes Secrets.

title: Container image management and provenance (APP.4.4.A2)
description: Container images must be sourced from trusted registries. Images must be scanned for known vulnerabilities before deployment and must not contain critical or high-severity CVEs. Images must be signed to provide provenance assurance. Base images must be updated with security patches within the patch management SLAs.
remediation_hint: Integrate container image scanning (Trivy, Grype, or equivalent) into the CI pipeline; block deployment of images with critical CVEs; enforce image signing with Cosign or equivalent.

title: Physical and logical access restrictions for servers (SYS.1.1.A1)
description: Physical access to server hardware must be restricted to authorised personnel. Logical access must be restricted to named administrators; interactive login with shared accounts is prohibited. Server consoles and management interfaces must be accessible only from defined management networks. Access must be logged.
remediation_hint: Implement physical access control to server locations; restrict management-plane access to a dedicated management VLAN; disable or remove console access routes not required for operations.

title: Minimal server configuration (SYS.1.1.A2)
description: Server operating systems must be configured with the minimum set of services, packages, and open network ports required for their function. All unnecessary services must be disabled or removed. The operating system must be hardened in accordance with a recognised baseline such as a CIS Benchmark or the BSI SiSyP hardening guide.
remediation_hint: Apply the CIS Benchmark for the server operating system; automate configuration baseline checks with a compliance scanner; remediate deviations within the patch management SLAs.

title: Restrictive authorisation for server access (SYS.1.1.A3)
description: Administrator privileges on servers must be granted only when required and must follow the principle of least privilege. Privilege escalation must use just-in-time or just-enough-access mechanisms where available. Root or local administrator login must be logged and, where possible, disabled in favour of named accounts with controlled privilege escalation.
remediation_hint: Disable direct root SSH login; use PAM or sudo with logging enabled for privilege escalation; alert on unexpected root access events in the SIEM.

title: Container security planning (SYS.1.6.A1)
description: A security concept for containerised deployments must be established before production rollout. The concept must address the full container lifecycle (build, ship, and run), the orchestration platform configuration, network isolation between containers, and secrets management. The concept must be reviewed when the platform or base images change significantly.
remediation_hint: Write and approve the container security concept before migrating workloads to containers; align with the APP.4.4 policy; review when the orchestration platform or base images change significantly.

title: Container image build security (SYS.1.6.A2)
description: Container images must be built from minimal base images, must not run as root by default, and must have a non-root user defined in the build specification. Multi-stage builds must be used to remove build-time artefacts and tooling from the production image. Image build pipelines must be version-controlled.
remediation_hint: Enforce a non-root USER directive in all Dockerfiles; use distroless or minimal base images; run image linting (hadolint or equivalent) in the CI pipeline.

title: Authorisation of container deployments (SYS.1.6.A5)
description: Container deployments to production must be authorised through the change management process. Only images that have passed security scanning and signing checks may be deployed to production. Deployment authorisation must be enforced by admission controls in the orchestration platform and logged.
remediation_hint: Deploy an admission controller (OPA/Gatekeeper, Kyverno, or equivalent) enforcing image signing and scan status before production admission; log all admission decisions.

title: Network architecture requirements (NET.1.1.A1)
description: A network architecture concept must be established defining network zones, trust boundaries, permitted traffic flows between zones, and the placement of security controls including firewalls, proxies, and load balancers. The architecture must follow the principle of need-to-connect. The concept must be kept current as the infrastructure evolves.
remediation_hint: Document the network architecture with zone definitions and permitted flows; validate the documentation against actual network configuration annually; review after every significant infrastructure change.

title: Network segmentation (NET.1.1.A2)
description: IT systems with different protection requirements must be separated into distinct network segments. Internet-facing components must be placed in a demilitarised zone (DMZ). Internal systems processing personal or confidential data must be isolated from general-purpose user networks and from each other where their protection requirements differ.
remediation_hint: Implement VLAN or virtual network segmentation; restrict lateral movement between segments with stateful firewall rules; verify segmentation with network scanning after changes.

title: Secure network management access (NET.1.1.A3)
description: Management access to network equipment must be restricted to a dedicated out-of-band management network or a hardened jump host. Remote management must use encrypted protocols (SSH or HTTPS) with multi-factor authentication. All management-plane access must be logged and reviewed periodically.
remediation_hint: Disable Telnet and unencrypted management protocols; route management access through a dedicated bastion or jump host; enforce MFA for all remote network management access.

title: Firewall security policy (NET.3.2.A1)
description: A documented firewall security policy must define the default-deny principle for traffic between security zones. Permitted traffic flows must be explicitly allowed on a need-to-communicate basis. The policy must be reviewed when application requirements change and the ruleset must be audited for redundant or overly permissive rules at least annually.
remediation_hint: Establish and approve the firewall ruleset against a written policy; audit the ruleset for shadowed or redundant rules annually; remove rules no longer required by an active application.

title: Stateful firewall implementation (NET.3.2.A2)
description: Stateful packet inspection firewalls must be deployed at all boundaries between network security zones. Firewall rules must block all traffic not explicitly permitted by the security policy. Firewall logging must capture all connection attempts including denied flows and must be retained and forwarded to the central logging system.
remediation_hint: Review and prune firewall rulesets quarterly; ensure denied flows are logged to the central SIEM; test firewall rules with automated network scanning after each significant rule change.

title: VPN security requirements (NET.3.3.A1)
description: Virtual private network (VPN) connections used for remote access or site-to-site connectivity must use only approved cryptographic algorithms and key lengths compliant with BSI TR-02102 or equivalent. VPN connections must require mutual authentication. Unused or inactive VPN accounts must be disabled within a defined inactivity period.
remediation_hint: Configure VPN gateways to allow only TLS 1.2+ or IKEv2 with BSI TR-02102-compliant cipher suites; enforce MFA for all remote-access VPN connections; automate deactivation of inactive VPN accounts.

title: Review of information security roles and responsibilities (ISMS.1.A2)
description: Information security roles, responsibilities, and delegated authorities must be reviewed at least annually to verify they remain appropriate as the organisation evolves. Role holders must re-confirm acceptance in writing after any significant change.
remediation_hint: Conduct and document an annual review of all information security roles; update the RACI when organisational changes occur; re-obtain written acceptance from role holders when responsibilities change significantly.

title: System-specific security concepts for IT systems (ISMS.1.A5)
description: Each IT system or group of comparable systems in scope must have a system-specific security concept derived from IT-Grundschutz modelling. The concept must document protection requirements, applicable Bausteine, implemented measures, and approved deviations.
remediation_hint: Complete IT-Grundschutz modelling for each IT system in scope; document the resulting security concept with implemented measures and approved deviations; review the concept when the system changes significantly.

title: Information security advice for projects and procurements (ISMS.1.A7)
description: The information security officer must be consulted on all projects and procurements that could have a material impact on information security, before decisions are made. The ISO must provide formal sign-off at key decision points.
remediation_hint: Establish a formal consultation process requiring ISO involvement at project initiation and procurement stages; document the ISO assessment and sign-off; track outstanding security requirements as project milestones.

title: Supervisory responsibility for information security (ORP.1.A3)
description: Supervisors at all levels must ensure that staff under their responsibility fulfil their information security obligations and are appropriately trained. Non-compliance must be addressed promptly and documented. Supervisors must themselves participate in security awareness activities.
remediation_hint: Include information security responsibilities in supervisor job descriptions; require supervisors to attend security awareness sessions; define a process for supervisors to report and address staff non-compliance.

title: Formal notification of staff obligations (ORP.1.A5)
description: All staff must be formally notified of their information security obligations in writing. The notification must cover applicable policies, acceptable use rules, and consequences of non-compliance. Staff must acknowledge receipt and understanding; acknowledgements must be retained and refreshed at defined intervals.
remediation_hint: Issue and record a formal security obligations acknowledgement for every employee and contractor; integrate the acknowledgement into the onboarding process; refresh annually.

title: Secure return of equipment and credentials on departure (ORP.2.A3)
description: All institutional equipment, credentials, access cards, and keys must be formally returned by departing staff before or at the point of departure. Return completion must be documented and confirmed by an authorised manager or HR representative.
remediation_hint: Add an equipment and credential return checklist to the offboarding procedure; require manager confirmation of completed return before departure; escalate non-returns to the information security officer within 24 hours.

title: Hardware security module for key storage (CON.1.A3)
description: Cryptographic keys protecting sensitive or personal data must be stored in a hardware security module (HSM) or an equivalent hardware-protected key store. Software-only key storage is not permitted for keys that protect confidential or higher-classified data.
remediation_hint: Migrate sensitive data encryption keys to an HSM or cloud-provider hardware-backed KMS; document which key classes are hardware-protected; prohibit software-only key storage for keys protecting confidential data.

title: Secure deletion and destruction of data (CON.1.A5)
description: Data that is no longer required must be securely deleted or physically destroyed using a procedure appropriate to the sensitivity of the data. Simple file deletion is not sufficient for confidential data. Deletion and destruction events must be documented.
remediation_hint: Implement a secure deletion policy specifying the required method per data classification; verify that storage media is overwritten or cryptographically erased before disposal; maintain a deletion log for sensitive data assets.

title: Physical and logical protection of backup media (CON.3.A4)
description: Backup media must be stored in a physically secured location with access controlled and logged separately from the primary system. Logical access to backup repositories must be restricted to authorised personnel. Remote access must be protected by additional measures.
remediation_hint: Restrict physical access to backup media to an authorised set; maintain an access log; require multi-factor authentication for remote access to backup repositories; review access controls annually.

title: Backup media rotation and off-site storage (CON.3.A5)
description: A media rotation scheme must be defined and implemented for tape or removable backup media. At least one backup copy must be stored off-site at all times. The off-site location must provide physical and environmental security equivalent to the primary backup storage.
remediation_hint: Define and document the rotation schedule; confirm that at least one current off-site copy exists; verify that the off-site location meets the same physical security standard as primary backup storage; test off-site retrieval annually.

title: Post-change evaluation (OPS.1.1.2.A4)
description: After completing a change, a formal evaluation must be performed to verify that the objectives of the change were met and that no unintended side-effects occurred. Changes to security-relevant components must include a specific security verification step.
remediation_hint: Add a mandatory post-change evaluation step to the change management process; require independent sign-off on the evaluation; capture the outcome in the change record.

title: Centralised vulnerability tracking register (OPS.1.1.3.A4)
description: All identified vulnerabilities across IT systems in scope must be recorded in a centralised tracking register with current remediation status, assigned owner, and target completion date. The register must be reviewed at least weekly; overdue critical vulnerabilities must be escalated to the information security officer immediately.
remediation_hint: Deploy a vulnerability management tool to centralise tracking; require all confirmed vulnerabilities to be recorded within 24 hours; automate escalation for items approaching their target remediation date.

title: Backup failure response plans (OPS.1.1.5.A2)
description: Documented plans must define the procedures to be followed in the event of a backup failure, including immediate response steps, escalation path, and contingency measures to minimise data loss until the backup capability is restored.
remediation_hint: Write and approve a backup failure response procedure; include it in the operations runbook; test the procedure as part of the annual BCP test; update based on test findings.

title: Cloud service exit planning (OPS.2.2.A5)
description: A documented exit plan must be maintained for each critical cloud service, defining the procedures, timelines, technical steps, and personnel required to migrate away from the service. The plan must address data portability, service continuity during transition, and contract termination requirements.
remediation_hint: Document an exit plan for each critical cloud service; verify data portability by testing export and import of representative data; review the exit plan annually and at each contract renewal.

title: Regular analysis of log data (DER.1.A4)
description: Collected security log data must be regularly analysed to identify patterns, anomalies, and potential indicators of compromise. Log analysis must be documented; findings that indicate a security event must trigger the incident management process.
remediation_hint: Establish a weekly or continuous log review process; document analysis findings; configure automated correlation rules to identify multi-event patterns; ensure trained personnel perform or supervise log analysis.

title: Automated real-time event detection (DER.1.A5)
description: Automated mechanisms must be deployed to detect security-relevant events in real time without depending on manual log review. Detection rules must be tuned to reduce false positives while maintaining sensitivity to genuine threats. Alert rules must be reviewed and tested at regular intervals.
remediation_hint: Deploy a SIEM or equivalent automated detection platform; implement and tune detection rules for the defined threat model; test alert rules against synthetic events at least quarterly; document tuning decisions.

title: IT forensics capability for incident investigation (DER.2.1.A4)
description: The institution must maintain or have contractual access to IT forensics capability for investigating security incidents. A forensic procedure must define how evidence is collected, preserved, and documented without contamination. First-responder staff must be trained in evidence preservation.
remediation_hint: Establish or contract IT forensics capability before it is needed; document the forensic evidence preservation procedure; train first-responder staff; verify capability through at least one dry-run exercise per year.

title: Verification of audit finding remediation (DER.3.1.A3)
description: All findings from information security audits must be subject to a formal follow-up verification to confirm that remediation actions were completed within agreed timeframes. The follow-up verification must be independent of the team that performed the remediation.
remediation_hint: Include a formal follow-up verification step in the audit lifecycle; assign verification to an independent auditor; report verification results to management; escalate findings remaining open beyond the agreed remediation date.

title: Business continuity testing with third parties (DER.4.A3)
description: Business continuity tests must include participation of key third-party service providers and critical supply chain partners where their services are material to recovery. The joint test must verify the third party's recovery capabilities and communication procedures under simulated disruption conditions.
remediation_hint: Identify critical third-party dependencies in the BCP; invite key service providers to participate in the annual continuity test; document their participation and test outcomes; track and resolve gaps identified during joint exercises.

title: Secure session management for web applications (APP.3.1.A4)
description: Web applications must implement secure session management including cryptographically strong session token generation, binding of sessions to user context, timeout after inactivity, and secure invalidation on logout. Session tokens must not be exposed in URLs.
remediation_hint: Implement session management using a well-reviewed library; configure session timeout at 30 minutes of inactivity or less; verify that logout invalidates the server-side session; test session fixation and hijacking resistance in security acceptance.

title: Logging of security events in web applications (APP.3.1.A5)
description: Web applications must log security-relevant events including authentication attempts, access control failures, and input validation errors. Logs must be structured, timestamped, and forwarded to the central logging system. Application logs must not capture sensitive values such as passwords or tokens.
remediation_hint: Configure application-level logging for all defined security event classes; verify that logs are forwarded to the SIEM; confirm that sensitive values are excluded from logs; test logging coverage as part of security acceptance.

title: Database activity monitoring (APP.4.3.A4)
description: Access to sensitive data in databases must be monitored for unusual or anomalous patterns. Database activity monitoring must cover both application-tier queries and direct DBA access. Alerts must be generated for bulk data extraction, privilege escalation, and access outside normal business patterns.
remediation_hint: Deploy database activity monitoring for all databases storing personal or sensitive data; define baseline normal access patterns; configure alerts for anomalous access; forward DAM logs to the central SIEM.

title: Encryption at rest for databases (APP.4.3.A5)
description: Databases storing sensitive or personal data must be protected by encryption at rest. Encryption keys must be managed separately from the encrypted data and must not be stored on the same infrastructure as the database host.
remediation_hint: Enable transparent data encryption or equivalent for all databases holding personal data; store encryption keys in an HSM or cloud-managed key service separate from the database host; verify encryption coverage in each audit cycle.

title: Runtime security monitoring for containers (APP.4.4.A3)
description: Container workloads must be monitored for anomalous behaviour at runtime. Runtime security controls must detect unexpected process execution, network connections, and file system modifications within running containers.
remediation_hint: Deploy a container runtime security tool; define baseline behavioural profiles for each container workload; configure alerts for deviations; forward runtime alerts to the SIEM.

title: Host-based network filtering for servers (SYS.1.1.A4)
description: A host-based firewall or equivalent host-level filtering mechanism must be deployed on all servers to restrict inbound and outbound network connections to only those explicitly required for the server's function. Default-deny rules must be applied at the host level.
remediation_hint: Enable and configure host-based firewall rules on all servers; document permitted connection flows; verify that host-level rules are consistent with network-level controls; review annually.

title: Physical environment protection for server hardware (SYS.1.1.A5)
description: Server hardware must be protected against environmental hazards including overheating, humidity, and power fluctuations. Environmental monitoring must be in place with automated alerting on threshold breach. Uninterruptible power supplies must be installed for servers where continuous availability is required.
remediation_hint: Install environmental monitoring with automated alerts; document UPS coverage for critical servers; test UPS failover at least annually; review environmental controls when the data centre configuration changes.

title: Container network policies (SYS.1.6.A3)
description: Kubernetes network policies or equivalent must restrict pod-to-pod communication to only explicitly permitted connections. A default-deny network policy must be applied at the namespace level. Network policy configuration must be version-controlled alongside the application manifests.
remediation_hint: Deploy and enforce a default-deny Kubernetes NetworkPolicy in all production namespaces; explicitly allow only required pod connections; audit network policy coverage with a policy validator; review when services are added or modified.

title: Read-only container filesystems (SYS.1.6.A4)
description: Container filesystems must be mounted read-only where technically feasible. Any write operations required by the container must be directed to explicitly defined writable volumes. Running containers must not be modified after deployment.
remediation_hint: Set readOnlyRootFilesystem: true in container security contexts; define explicit writable volumes only where required; enforce this setting via admission control policy; verify compliance in the CI pipeline image configuration check.

title: Network path redundancy for critical infrastructure (NET.1.1.A4)
description: Critical network paths must be designed with redundancy to eliminate single points of failure. Where redundancy cannot be achieved, identified single points of failure must be documented as residual risks with compensating controls. Network failover mechanisms must be tested at defined intervals.
remediation_hint: Document network topology with identified single points of failure; implement redundant paths for critical links; test failover mechanisms annually; track unresolved single points of failure as risks in the risk register.

title: Filtering between internal security zones (NET.1.1.A5)
description: Security controls equivalent in function to a firewall must be deployed at all boundaries between internal security zones. Lateral movement between internal zones must be filtered to only explicitly permitted flows. Internal zone boundary controls must be monitored, logged, and reviewed annually.
remediation_hint: Deploy stateful filtering at all internal zone boundaries; enforce default-deny between zones; monitor and log inter-zone traffic; review internal zone firewall rules as part of the annual network security audit.

title: Intrusion detection and prevention system deployment (NET.3.2.A3)
description: Intrusion detection or prevention systems must be deployed at critical network boundaries to detect and optionally block known attack patterns. IDS/IPS signatures and behavioural models must be kept current. Detection alerts must be forwarded to the central logging system.
remediation_hint: Deploy network IDS/IPS at DMZ and data centre ingress boundaries; maintain up-to-date signature feeds; forward alerts to the SIEM; review IDS/IPS configuration and alert tuning quarterly.

title: Firewall penetration testing (NET.3.2.A4)
description: Firewall configurations must be subject to regular penetration testing or independent technical security review to verify that the implemented rules enforce the security policy and that no unintended access paths exist.
remediation_hint: Schedule annual firewall penetration testing or independent ruleset review; remediate all critical and high findings within the patch management SLA; document test results and present them to the information security officer.

title: VPN connection event logging (NET.3.3.A2)
description: All VPN connection events must be logged including successful connections, failed authentication attempts, and session terminations. Logs must include timestamps, user or device identifiers, and source IP addresses. VPN logs must be forwarded to the central logging system.
remediation_hint: Enable and configure VPN gateway logging for all event types; verify log forwarding to the SIEM; confirm that logs capture all required fields; set retention to meet the minimum required period.
